questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
What is net force?
choices: The vector sum of all forces acting on an object
An object's mass divided by time
The largest single force, ignoring all others
The number of surfaces touching an object

questions.question: What is inertia?
choices: A force produced only by friction

questions.question: Which relationship expresses Newton's second law for constant mass?
What is weight?
choices: The gravitational force acting on an object
The amount of matter in an object

questions.question: Which force is a surface's push perpendicular to that surface?
What does Newton's third law describe?
choices: Equal and opposite interaction forces acting on different objects
A force always pointing in the direction of motion
Two equal forces acting on the same object only

questions.question: What motion is possible when the net force on an object is zero?
Why is greater force needed to produce the same acceleration in a more massive object?
choices: Greater mass automatically reduces the needed force
Greater mass always means lower friction
Force is independent of mass for equal acceleration

questions.question: Why do third-law force pairs not cancel each other when analyzing one object's net force?
choices: Only one member is a real force
The pair acts on different objects

questions.question: How does friction commonly affect sliding motion?
choices: It always increases speed in the direction of sliding
It opposes the relative sliding of contacting surfaces
It acts only without surface contact

questions.question: How do mass and weight differ?
choices: Mass describes matter and inertia; weight is a gravitational force
Mass depends only on location; weight never does
Mass is measured in newtons; weight in kilograms
They are interchangeable in every physical equation

questions.question: Why does a passenger continue forward when a vehicle stops suddenly?
choices: The vehicle creates a new forward gravitational force
The passenger's inertia resists the change in motion
All forces disappear inside the vehicle

questions.question: What does a seat belt do during a sudden stop?
choices: It makes the passenger's weight vanish
It prevents the vehicle from having acceleration
It exerts a force that changes the passenger's motion

questions.question: Why does an object moving in a circle require a net inward force?
choices: Its mass must increase every second

questions.question: A 2 kg object has a net force of 10 N. What is its acceleration?
A box experiences 8 N rightward and 3 N leftward. What is the net force?
A book rests on a level table. Which pair of forces on the book balances in this situation?
choices: The book's weight and its pull on Earth
The book's weight and the table's normal force
The table's normal force and the book's push on the table
The book's inertia and Earth's inertia

questions.question: A swimmer pushes water backward. What third-law effect helps the swimmer move forward?
choices: The swimmer's weight turns into forward speed
The swimmer experiences no external force
The water pushes the swimmer forward

questions.question: An astronaut moves from Earth to a place with weaker gravity. What happens to mass and weight?
choices: Mass decreases while weight stays the same
Mass stays the same while weight decreases
